lead_in: Any one of these works (you only need one):
question_text: Name one power that is only for the states.

why_it_matters.text: Some powers stay with the states because local needs are different. A city in Wyoming faces different problems than New York City. The framers thought decisions about schools, police, and zoning should be made close to home — by people who actually live there — not by far-away officials in Washington.

fun_fact.text: Schools, police, and fire departments are state and local jobs — not federal. That's why a 2nd grader in Minnesota might read different books, learn different math methods, and take different tests than a 2nd grader in Florida. The U.S. has 50 separate state education systems and thousands of local school districts deciding what to teach.
